items.title: Dependent-Origination-Skillfulness: Craving as What Waters the Seeds

items.zh: 云何緣起？云何緣起善巧？謂無明緣行，行緣識，識緣名色，名色緣六處，六處緣觸，觸緣受，受緣愛，愛緣取，取緣有，有緣生，生緣老死，乃至招集如是純大苦蘊。是名緣起。若復了知唯有諸法滋潤諸法，唯有諸法等潤諸法，唯有諸行引發諸行；而彼諸行因所生故、緣所生故，本無而有，有已散滅，體是無常。是無常故，即是生法，老法，病法，死法，愁、悴、悲、嘆、憂、苦、惱法；是生法故，乃至是惱法故，則名為苦。由是苦故，不得自在，其力羸劣，由是因緣，定無有我。若於如是緣生法中，由如是等種種行相，善巧了達，或無常智、或苦智、或無我智，是名緣起善巧。
items.en: What is dependent origination? What is skillfulness regarding it? Ignorance conditions volitional formations; formations condition consciousness; consciousness conditions name-and-form; name-and-form conditions the six sense-bases; the six sense-bases condition contact; contact conditions feeling; feeling conditions craving; craving conditions grasping; grasping conditions becoming; becoming conditions birth; birth conditions ageing and death — thus gathering this whole mass of suffering. This is called dependent origination. Further knowing that only phenomena water other phenomena, only phenomena evenly saturate other phenomena, only formations draw forth further formations — and that these formations, being produced by causes and by conditions, are non-existent and then exist, and having existed then dissolve — their nature is impermanent. Being impermanent, this is subject to birth, ageing, sickness, and death … and is therefore called suffering. Being suffering, it lacks autonomy, its power feeble and weak — and by this very reasoning, there is definitely no self. Skilfully realising, within phenomena thus arisen from conditions, the wisdom of impermanence, or the wisdom of suffering, or the wisdom of non-self — this is called skillfulness regarding dependent origination.

items.title: Section: Possible-and-Impossible-Skillfulness Closes All Five Skilful Objects

items.zh: 又處非處善巧，當知即是緣起善巧差別。此中差別者，謂由處非處善巧故，能正了知非不平等因果道理。則善不善法有果異熟。若諸善法能感可愛果異熟法，諸不善法能感非愛果異熟法。若能如是如實了知，名處非處善巧。此五善巧略則為二。一、自相善巧，二、共相善巧。
items.en: Skillfulness regarding what is possible and impossible should be known as simply a further distinction within skillfulness regarding dependent origination. The distinction here is this: through this skillfulness, one correctly knows that the principle of cause and effect is never unequal — that wholesome and unwholesome actions each have their own ripened result. Wholesome actions bring about a desirable ripened result; unwholesome actions bring about an undesirable ripened result. Truly knowing this is called skillfulness regarding what is possible and impossible. … These five skillfulnesses, briefly, reduce to two: skillfulness regarding particular characteristics, and skillfulness regarding shared characteristics.

items.zh: 由蘊善巧顯自相善巧；由餘善巧顯共相善巧。如是總名善巧所緣。

items.title: Section: Purifying-of-Affliction Objects Open — the Mundane Path

items.zh: 云何淨惑所緣？謂觀下地麁性、上地靜性。如欲界對初靜慮，乃至無所有處對非想非非想處。云何麁性？謂麁性有二。一、體麁性，二、數麁性。體麁性者，謂欲界望初靜慮，雖皆具五蘊，而欲界中過患深重，苦住增上，最為鄙劣，甚可厭惡，是故說彼為體麁性。初靜慮中則不如是，極靜、極妙，是故說彼為體靜性。數麁性者，謂欲界色蘊有多品類，應知應斷，如是乃至識蘊亦爾，是故說彼為數麁性。如是上地展轉相望，若體麁性、若數麁性，隨其所應，當知亦爾。如是麁性，於諸上地展轉相望，乃至極於無所有處，一切下地苦惱增多，壽量減少；一切上地苦惱減少，壽量增多。非想非非想處唯靜、唯妙，更無上地勝過此故。以要言之，有過患義是麁性義。若彼彼地中過患增多，即由如是過患增多性故，名為麁性。若彼彼地中過患減少，即由如是過患減少性故，名為靜性。此是世間由世俗道淨惑所緣。何以故？彼觀下地多諸過患，如病、如癰，猶如毒箭，不安隱性，以為麁性；觀於上地與彼相違，以為靜性。
items.en: What are purifying-of-affliction objects? It is contemplating the coarseness of the lower level and the calm of the level above it — the desire realm compared against the first absorption, and so on up through the sphere of nothing-whatsoever compared against the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. Regarding coarseness of substance: comparing the desire realm to the first absorption, though both possess the five aggregates, the desire realm's faults and defects run deep, dwelling constantly in suffering, the basest and most contemptible of states, thoroughly worthy of aversion — hence it is called coarse in substance. … Stated briefly, having the quality of fault and defect is what "coarseness" means. Wherever faults and defects increase, by that very increase it is called coarse; wherever they decrease, by that very decrease it is called calm.

items.title: Section: Only Temporary — the Warning of Udraka Rāmaputra

items.zh: 斷除下地所有煩惱，始從欲界乃至上極無所有處。此是暫斷，非究竟斷。以於後時、更相續故。
items.en: The afflictions of each lower level, from the desire realm all the way up to the sphere of nothing-whatsoever, are cut off by this method — but this is only a temporary cutting-off, not a final one, since these afflictions arise again afterwards in continuity.

items.title: Section: The Supramundane Path Opens — Suffering and Its Origin

items.zh: 出世間道淨惑所緣復有四種。一、苦聖諦，二、集聖諦，三、滅聖諦，四、道聖諦。云何苦聖諦？謂生苦、老苦、病苦、死苦、怨憎會苦、愛別離苦、求不得苦、略說一切五取蘊苦、名苦聖諦。云何集聖諦？謂若愛、若後有愛、若喜貪俱行愛、若彼彼喜樂愛等，名集聖諦。
items.en: The supramundane path's purifying-of-affliction objects are of four kinds: the noble truth of suffering, of its origin, of its cessation, and of the path. What is the noble truth of suffering? Birth, ageing, sickness, and death; meeting the disliked; parting from the loved; not obtaining what is sought; and, in brief, the suffering of the five aggregates of grasping altogether — this is the noble truth of suffering. What is the noble truth of the origin? It is self-love, love of future existence, craving bound up with delight in what is presently held dear, and longing-craving for what is not yet obtained — these are the noble truth of the origin.

items.title: Section: Cessation, Path, and the Black-and-White Framework Close the Four Truths

items.zh: 云何滅聖諦？謂即此愛等無餘斷滅，名滅聖諦。云何道聖諦？謂八支等聖道，名道聖諦。當知此中，依黑品白品果因建立故，建立四聖諦。謂苦諦是黑品果；集諦是黑品因；滅諦是白品果；道諦是白品因，能得、能證故。
items.en: What is the noble truth of cessation? It is the complete, remainderless ending of this very craving — this is the noble truth of cessation. What is the noble truth of the path? It is the eightfold noble path and its allied factors — this is the noble truth of the path. Know that these four noble truths are established according to the relation of cause and effect within the tainted and the pure: the truth of suffering is the tainted effect; the truth of origin is the tainted cause; the truth of cessation is the pure effect; and the truth of the path is the pure cause, since it is what attains and what realises cessation.

blocks.text: The last two skilful objects, then the fourth category: objects for **purifying affliction**, by the mundane and supramundane paths.

"Only phenomena water other phenomena, only formations draw forth further formations." Craving waters the seeds. "Being suffering, it lacks autonomy, its power feeble; by this very reasoning, there is definitely no self."
A further distinction within dependent origination: "one correctly knows that the principle of cause and effect is never unequal": good deeds do not bring bad results, nor bad deeds good ones.
One contemplates "the coarseness of the lower level and the calm of the level above": desire realm against the first absorption, and so on. Master Cháng Bǎi: this is relative purity.

"This is only a temporary cutting-off, not a final one, since these afflictions arise again." The treatise recalls Udraka Rāmaputra, who reached the peak of existence and was reborn there, but whose afflictions remained. Master Cháng Bǎi adds a hopeful note: even Devadatta, who fell into Avīci, will in time attain awakening.

**Suffering**: "birth, ageing, sickness, death; meeting the disliked; parting from the loved; not obtaining what is sought; in brief, the five aggregates of grasping". **Origin**: craving for future existence, accompanied by delight and lust, delighting here and there. **Cessation**: "the complete, remainderless ending of this very craving". **Path**: the eightfold path.
The truth of suffering is the tainted effect; origin, the tainted cause; cessation, the pure effect; path, the pure cause.

quiz.q: What does skill in dependent origination know, and what image does Master Cháng Bǎi use for "watering"?
options: only phenomena water and saturate phenomena, formations draw forth formations, arising and dissolving; karmic seeds bear fruit only when watered by craving and grasping
quiz.why: "Only phenomena water other phenomena, only phenomena evenly saturate other phenomena, only formations draw forth further formations … non-existent and then exist, and having existed then dissolve." Master Cháng Bǎi: the karmic seeds stored in consciousness must be nourished and watered by craving and grasping before they manifest as fruit.

quiz.q: The text reasons "being suffering, lacking autonomy … there is definitely no self." How does Venerable Miào Jìng move from suffering to non-self?
options: if there were a self, it would be autonomous and strong, and would not suffer
quiz.why: "Being suffering, it lacks autonomy, its power feeble and weak — and by this very reasoning, there is definitely no self." Venerable Miào Jìng: if there were a self, it would be autonomous, would have power, and would not suffer.

quiz.q: What does skill in the possible and impossible know, and what does Master Cháng Bǎi give as an "unequal cause"?
options: cause and effect is never unequal — wholesome brings desirable results, unwholesome undesirable; saying all things come from God while God simply exists is unequal
quiz.why: "Through this skillfulness, one correctly knows that the principle of cause and effect is never unequal." Master Cháng Bǎi: if God created all things, things would exist by causes while God exists by itself — that is unequal.

quiz.q: To what kind of karma does Venerable Miào Jìng assign the mundane path's purifying objects?
options: beyond wrongdoing and merit — imperturbable karma
quiz.why: "What are purifying-of-affliction objects? It is contemplating the coarseness of the lower level and the calm of the level above it." Venerable Miào Jìng: this purifying object goes beyond wrongdoing and merit; it belongs to imperturbable karma.

quiz.q: What kind of cutting-off does the mundane path achieve, and why, according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: only temporary — afflictions return; concentration is time-bound, and when lost, the lower afflictions reappear
quiz.why: "This is only a temporary cutting-off, not a final one, since these afflictions arise again afterwards in continuity." Venerable Miào Jìng: the concentration you achieve is time-bound; when it is lost, the afflictions of the lower level reappear.

quiz.q: On the mundane path's temporary cutting, the note cites Devadatta "committing the five most heinous crimes." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say of Devadatta, and what does Venerable Miào Jìng warn?
options: Cháng Bǎi: Devadatta committed three of the heinous deeds, fell to Avīci, and will attain solitary awakening when lifespans are forty thousand years; Miào Jìng: what becomes of one who sits only for calm without insight?
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: though Devadatta committed three heinous deeds, cut his roots of virtue, and fell into Avīci, he will attain solitary awakening when the human lifespan is forty thousand years. Venerable Miào Jìng: if in sitting we don't cultivate insight but only crave inner calm, what will become of us? The note says five crimes; the lecture, three.

quiz.q: What sufferings make up the noble truth of suffering, and how does Venerable Miào Jìng divide particular from general?
options: birth, ageing, sickness, death, meeting the disliked, parting from the loved, not getting what one seeks, and in brief the five aggregates of grasping; the seven are particular, the last general — eight in all
quiz.why: "Birth, ageing, sickness, and death; meeting the disliked; parting from the loved; not obtaining what is sought; and, in brief, the suffering of the five aggregates of grasping." Venerable Miào Jìng: the first seven are stated individually, the five aggregates of grasping in general; together, eight sufferings.
